_about: Innervation, action and blood supply for muscles the dataset leaves without innervation. Nerve names that match an atlas nerve become links. See app/extra_content.py.

Abductor pollicis longus.action: Abducts and extends the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint; assists radial deviation of the wrist.

Extensor pollicis brevis.action: Extends the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal and carpometacarpal joints; assists abduction.

Extensor pollicis longus.action: Extends the thumb at the interphalangeal, metacarpophalangeal and carpometacarpal joints; retropulsion of the thumb.

Extensor indicis.action: Extends the index finger independently (pointing); assists wrist extension.

Extensor digitorum.action: Extends the fingers at the metacarpophalangeal joints and, through the extensor expansions, the interphalangeal joints; assists wrist extension.
Extensor digitorum.blood_supply: Posterior interosseous and radial recurrent arteries.

Extensor digiti minimi.action: Extends the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints.

Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnaris.action: With the ulnar head: extends and adducts (ulnar-deviates) the wrist.

Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris.action: With the humeral head: extends and adducts (ulnar-deviates) the wrist.

Supinator.action: Supinates the forearm, especially with the elbow extended (biceps supinates the flexed elbow).
Supinator.blood_supply: Radial recurrent and recurrent interosseous arteries.

Radial head of flexor digitorum superfic.action: With the humero-ulnar head: flexes the fingers at the proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints; assists wrist flexion.

Subscapularis muscle.action: Medially rotates the humerus; as part of the rotator cuff holds the humeral head in the glenoid and resists anterior dislocation.
Subscapularis muscle.blood_supply: Subscapular, suprascapular and transverse cervical arteries.

Teres major muscle.action: Adducts, medially rotates and extends the humerus.

Latissimus dorsi muscle.action: Extends, adducts and medially rotates the humerus; raises the trunk toward the arms in climbing; assists forced expiration and coughing.
Latissimus dorsi muscle.blood_supply: Thoracodorsal artery (dominant pedicle), plus posterior intercostal and lumbar perforators.

Pectoralis minor muscle.action: Draws the scapula forward and downward against the chest wall; raises the ribs in forced inspiration when the scapula is fixed.
Pectoralis minor muscle.blood_supply: Pectoral branches of the thoraco-acromial artery and the lateral thoracic artery.

Diaphragm.action: Main muscle of inspiration: contraction flattens the domes, enlarging the thorax vertically; also raises intra-abdominal pressure for defaecation, micturition and parturition.
Diaphragm.blood_supply: Superior and inferior phrenic, musculophrenic, pericardiacophrenic and lower posterior intercostal arteries.

External intercostal muscles.action: Elevate the ribs in inspiration; keep the intercostal spaces from bulging or being sucked in.

Internal intercostal muscles.action: The interosseous parts depress the ribs in forced expiration; the interchondral parts help elevate them in inspiration.
Internal intercostal muscles.blood_supply: Posterior and anterior intercostal arteries and the musculophrenic artery.

Innermost intercostal muscles.action: Act with the internal intercostals; the intercostal vessels and nerve run between them and the internal intercostals.

Transversus thoracis muscle.action: Weakly depresses the costal cartilages in expiration.

Serratus posterior superior muscle.action: Elevates the 2nd to 5th ribs; its role in breathing is minor and it may be mainly proprioceptive.

Serratus posterior inferior muscle.action: Draws the lower four ribs down and back, resisting the pull of the diaphragm.
Serratus posterior inferior muscle.blood_supply: Posterior intercostal, subcostal and lumbar arteries.

innervation: Dorsal rami of C8-T11 spinal nerves
Levatores breves costarum.action: Elevate the ribs; assist lateral flexion and rotation of the thoracic spine.

innervation: Dorsal rami of C8-T11 spinal nerves
Levatores longi costarum.action: Elevate the ribs; assist lateral flexion and rotation of the thoracic spine.

External abdominal oblique muscle.action: Compresses the abdomen; bilaterally flexes the trunk; unilaterally bends it to the same side and rotates it to the opposite side.
External abdominal oblique muscle.blood_supply: Lower posterior intercostal, subcostal, superior and inferior epigastric and deep circumflex iliac arteries.

Internal abdominal oblique muscle.action: Compresses the abdomen; bilaterally flexes the trunk; unilaterally bends and rotates it to the same side. Its lowest fibres form the conjoint tendon and cremaster.
Internal abdominal oblique muscle.blood_supply: Lower posterior intercostal, superior and inferior epigastric and deep circumflex iliac arteries.

Transversus abdominis muscle.action: Compresses the abdominal contents and, with the thoracolumbar fascia, stabilises the lumbar spine before limb movement.
Transversus abdominis muscle.blood_supply: Lower posterior intercostal, deep circumflex iliac and superior and inferior epigastric arteries.

Rectus abdominis muscle.action: Flexes the trunk (lumbar spine); compresses the abdomen; stabilises and tilts the pelvis backward.
Rectus abdominis muscle.blood_supply: Superior and inferior epigastric arteries (the inferior is the dominant pedicle of TRAM/DIEP flaps).

Pyramidalis muscle.action: Tenses the linea alba. Absent in about 20% of people.

Quadratus lumborum muscle.action: Bends the trunk to the same side; fixes the 12th rib in inspiration; bilaterally extends the lumbar spine; hitches the hip up in gait.

Psoas major.action: With iliacus (iliopsoas) the most powerful flexor of the hip; flexes the trunk on the thigh (sitting up) and laterally flexes the lumbar spine.
Psoas major.blood_supply: Lumbar arteries and the lumbar branch of the iliolumbar artery.

Gluteus maximus muscle.action: Powerful extensor and lateral rotator of the hip, used in climbing, running and rising from sitting; through the iliotibial tract steadies the extended knee.
Gluteus maximus muscle.blood_supply: Superior and inferior gluteal arteries; first perforating artery.

Gluteus medius muscle.action: Abducts and medially rotates the hip; in single-leg stance keeps the pelvis level (weakness gives a Trendelenburg sign).

Gluteus minimus muscle.action: Abducts and medially rotates the hip; stabilises the pelvis in single-leg stance with gluteus medius.

Tensor fasciae latae.action: Abducts, medially rotates and flexes the hip; tenses the iliotibial tract to stabilise the extended knee.
Tensor fasciae latae.blood_supply: Ascending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery and superior gluteal artery.

Piriformis muscle.action: Laterally rotates the extended hip and abducts the flexed hip; stabilises the femoral head in the acetabulum.
Piriformis muscle.blood_supply: Superior and inferior gluteal arteries and internal pudendal artery.

Superior gemellus muscle.action: With obturator internus laterally rotates the extended hip and abducts the flexed hip.
Superior gemellus muscle.blood_supply: Inferior gluteal and internal pudendal arteries.

Inferior gemellus muscle.action: With obturator internus laterally rotates the extended hip and abducts the flexed hip.
Inferior gemellus muscle.blood_supply: Medial circumflex femoral and inferior gluteal arteries.

Quadratus femoris muscle.action: Laterally rotates the hip and holds the femoral head in the acetabulum.

Obturator externus.action: Laterally rotates the hip and steadies the femoral head.
Obturator externus.blood_supply: Obturator and medial circumflex femoral arteries.

Adductor minimus.action: Adducts and laterally rotates the hip (the upper part of adductor magnus).
Adductor minimus.blood_supply: Obturator, medial circumflex femoral and first perforating arteries.

Coccygeus muscle.action: Supports the pelvic floor with levator ani and pulls the coccyx forward after defaecation or parturition.
Coccygeus muscle.blood_supply: Inferior gluteal and internal pudendal arteries.

Iliococcygeus muscle.action: Part of levator ani: supports the pelvic viscera and raises the pelvic floor, resisting rises in intra-abdominal pressure.
Iliococcygeus muscle.blood_supply: Inferior gluteal, internal pudendal and inferior vesical arteries.

Pubococcygeus muscle.action: Part of levator ani: supports the pelvic viscera, constricts the urogenital and anal openings and helps maintain continence.
Pubococcygeus muscle.blood_supply: Inferior gluteal, internal pudendal and inferior vesical arteries.

Pubo-analis muscle.action: Fibres of pubococcygeus inserting into the anal canal wall between the sphincters; elevate the anal canal and assist continence.

External anal sphincter.action: Voluntary closure of the anal canal; its tonic contraction and the puborectalis sling maintain faecal continence.
External anal sphincter.blood_supply: Inferior rectal (anal) arteries from the internal pudendal artery.

innervation: Dorsal rami of cervical and upper thoracic spinal nerves
Iliocostalis colli muscle.action: Extends and laterally flexes the cervical spine.
Iliocostalis colli muscle.blood_supply: Deep cervical, occipital and vertebral arteries.

innervation: Dorsal rami of thoracic spinal nerves
Iliocostalis thoracis muscle.action: Extends and laterally flexes the thoracic spine; helps depress the ribs.
Iliocostalis thoracis muscle.blood_supply: Dorsal branches of the posterior intercostal arteries.

innervation: Dorsal rami of thoracic and lumbar spinal nerves
Iliocostalis lumborum muscle.action: Extends and laterally flexes the lumbar spine; depresses the lower ribs.
Iliocostalis lumborum muscle.blood_supply: Dorsal branches of the lumbar, subcostal and lower posterior intercostal arteries.

innervation: Dorsal rami of cervical spinal nerves
Longissimus capitis muscle.action: Extends the head; turns the face to the same side and laterally flexes the neck.
Longissimus capitis muscle.blood_supply: Occipital, deep cervical and vertebral arteries.

innervation: Dorsal rami of cervical and upper thoracic spinal nerves
Longissimus colli muscle.action: Extends and laterally flexes the cervical spine.

innervation: Dorsal rami of thoracic and lumbar spinal nerves
Longissimus thoracis muscle.action: Extends and laterally flexes the thoracic and lumbar spine; depresses the ribs.
Longissimus thoracis muscle.blood_supply: Dorsal branches of the posterior intercostal, subcostal and lumbar arteries.

innervation: Dorsal rami of cervical spinal nerves
Spinalis capitis muscle.action: Extends the head (usually blended with semispinalis capitis).

innervation: Dorsal rami of cervical spinal nerves
Dorsal rami of thoracic spinal nerves
Spinalis thoracis muscle.blood_supply: Dorsal branches of the posterior intercostal arteries.

innervation: Dorsal rami of cervical and thoracic spinal nerves
Semispinalis colli muscle.action: Extends the cervical and upper thoracic spine and rotates it to the opposite side.
Semispinalis colli muscle.blood_supply: Deep cervical and posterior intercostal arteries.

innervation: Dorsal rami of thoracic spinal nerves
Semispinalis thoracis muscle.action: Extends the thoracic spine and rotates it to the opposite side.
Semispinalis thoracis muscle.blood_supply: Dorsal branches of the posterior intercostal arteries.

Multifidus colli muscle.action: Stabilises adjacent vertebrae during movement; extends and rotates the neck to the opposite side.

Multifidus thoracis muscle.action: Stabilises adjacent vertebrae; extends and rotates the thoracic spine to the opposite side.
Multifidus thoracis muscle.blood_supply: Dorsal branches of the posterior intercostal arteries.

Multifidus lumborum muscle.action: Key segmental stabiliser of the lumbar spine; extends and rotates it to the opposite side. Often atrophied in chronic low back pain.
Multifidus lumborum muscle.blood_supply: Dorsal branches of the lumbar arteries.

Rotatores.action: Stabilise and rotate adjacent vertebrae to the opposite side; rich in muscle spindles, they act largely as position sensors.
Rotatores.blood_supply: Dorsal branches of the segmental (intercostal, lumbar, deep cervical) arteries.

Interspinales colli muscles.action: Extend the neck and stabilise adjacent spinous processes; mainly proprioceptive.

Interspinales thoracis muscles.action: Extend the spine between adjacent spinous processes; often present only at the ends of the thoracic region.
Interspinales thoracis muscles.blood_supply: Dorsal branches of the posterior intercostal arteries.

Interspinales lumborum muscles.action: Extend the lumbar spine and stabilise adjacent spinous processes; mainly proprioceptive.
Interspinales lumborum muscles.blood_supply: Dorsal branches of the lumbar arteries.

innervation: Dorsal rami of lumbar spinal nerves
Dorsal parts of lateral intertransversar.action: Assist lateral flexion and stabilise adjacent lumbar vertebrae.

innervation: Dorsal rami of middle cervical spinal nerves
Splenius capitis muscle.action: Bilaterally extends the head and neck; unilaterally bends the neck and turns the face to the same side.
Splenius capitis muscle.blood_supply: Muscular branches of the occipital artery and the transverse cervical artery.

innervation: Dorsal rami of lower cervical spinal nerves
Splenius colli muscle.action: Extends the neck; unilaterally bends and rotates it to the same side.

Rectus posterior major capitis muscle.action: Extends the head and rotates it to the same side at the atlanto-axial joint.

Rectus posterior minor capitis muscle.action: Extends the head at the atlanto-occipital joints; its connection to the dura may keep the dura taut.

Obliquus inferior capitis muscle.action: Rotates the atlas, and so the head, to the same side at the atlanto-axial joint.

Obliquus superior capitis muscle.action: Extends the head and bends it to the same side.

Longus capitis muscle.action: Flexes the head at the atlanto-occipital joints and flexes the upper cervical spine.
Longus capitis muscle.blood_supply: Ascending pharyngeal, ascending cervical and vertebral arteries.

Longus colli muscle.action: Flexes the cervical spine and resists its hyperextension; slight rotation and lateral flexion.
Longus colli muscle.blood_supply: Ascending cervical, inferior thyroid and vertebral arteries.

Scalenus anterior muscle.action: Elevates the first rib in forced inspiration; laterally flexes the neck and rotates it to the opposite side.
Scalenus anterior muscle.blood_supply: Ascending cervical branch of the inferior thyroid artery.

Scalenus medius muscle.action: Elevates the first rib in forced inspiration; laterally flexes the neck.
Scalenus medius muscle.blood_supply: Ascending cervical artery and muscular branches of the vertebral artery.

Scalenus posterior muscle.action: Elevates the second rib; laterally flexes the neck.

Platysma.action: Tenses the skin of the neck; depresses the mandible and draws down the corners of the mouth (expressions of horror or strain).
Platysma.blood_supply: Submental branch of the facial artery and suprascapular artery.

Omohyoid muscle.action: Depresses and steadies the hyoid bone after swallowing; may tense the carotid sheath.
Omohyoid muscle.blood_supply: Superior thyroid and transverse cervical arteries.

Sternohyoid muscle.action: Depresses the hyoid bone after it has been raised in swallowing and speech.

Sternothyroid muscle.action: Depresses the larynx (thyroid cartilage) after swallowing and in singing low notes.

innervation: C1 fibres via the hypoglossal nerve (XII)
Thyrohyoid muscle.action: Depresses the hyoid; with the hyoid fixed, raises the larynx.

innervation: C1 fibres via the hypoglossal nerve (XII)
Geniohyoid muscle.action: Pulls the hyoid bone forward and up in swallowing, widening the pharynx; with the hyoid fixed, depresses the mandible.
Geniohyoid muscle.blood_supply: Sublingual branch of the lingual artery.

Stylopharyngeus muscle.action: Elevates the pharynx and larynx and widens the pharynx during swallowing and speech. The only muscle supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve.

Superior pharyngeal constrictor.action: Constricts the upper pharynx in swallowing; forms Passavant's ridge that helps close the nasopharynx. Supplied via the pharyngeal plexus.
Superior pharyngeal constrictor.blood_supply: Ascending pharyngeal artery and tonsillar branch of the facial artery.

Middle pharyngeal constrictor.action: Constricts the middle pharynx, propelling the bolus downward. Supplied via the pharyngeal plexus.
Middle pharyngeal constrictor.blood_supply: Ascending pharyngeal artery and branches of the facial and lingual arteries.

Inferior pharyngeal constrictor.action: The thyropharyngeal part propels the bolus down; the cricopharyngeal part is the upper oesophageal sphincter, relaxing only in swallowing. A weak area between them (Killian's dehiscence) is where a Zenker diverticulum forms. Supplied via the pharyngeal plexus and the external and recurrent laryngeal nerves.
Inferior pharyngeal constrictor.blood_supply: Ascending pharyngeal, superior thyroid and inferior thyroid arteries.

Palatopharyngeus muscle.action: Elevates the pharynx and larynx and draws the palatopharyngeal arches together, closing the oropharyngeal isthmus in swallowing. Supplied via the pharyngeal plexus.
Palatopharyngeus muscle.blood_supply: Ascending pharyngeal, ascending palatine and greater palatine arteries.

Oblique part of cricothyroid muscle.action: Tilts the thyroid cartilage forward on the cricoid, lengthening and tensing the vocal folds to raise pitch. The only intrinsic laryngeal muscle not supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve.
Oblique part of cricothyroid muscle.blood_supply: Cricothyroid branch of the superior thyroid artery.

Straight part of cricothyroid muscle.action: Tilts the thyroid cartilage forward on the cricoid, lengthening and tensing the vocal folds to raise pitch.
Straight part of cricothyroid muscle.blood_supply: Cricothyroid branch of the superior thyroid artery.

Posterior crico-arytenoid muscle.action: The only abductor of the vocal folds: rotates the arytenoids laterally to open the rima glottidis. Bilateral paralysis threatens the airway.

Lateral crico-arytenoid muscle.action: Rotates the arytenoids medially, adducting the vocal folds (closing the intermembranous glottis) for phonation.

Transverse arytenoid muscle.action: Draws the arytenoid cartilages together, closing the posterior (intercartilaginous) part of the rima glottidis.

Ary-epiglottic part of oblique arytenoid.action: Continues the oblique arytenoid into the aryepiglottic fold; acts as a sphincter narrowing the laryngeal inlet in swallowing.

External part of thyro-arytenoid muscle.action: Draws the arytenoids forward, shortening and relaxing the vocal folds (lowering pitch); assists closure of the glottis.

Thyro-epiglottic part of thyro-arytenoid.action: Fibres that continue into the aryepiglottic fold and toward the epiglottis; act on the laryngeal inlet (usually described as widening it).

Lateral rectus muscle.action: Abducts the eye (turns the cornea laterally). Sixth nerve palsy gives a convergent squint and horizontal diplopia worse on looking to the affected side.
Lateral rectus muscle.blood_supply: Lacrimal artery and muscular branches of the ophthalmic artery.

Superior oblique muscle.action: Intorts the eye; depresses it, especially when the eye is adducted (looking down and in, as in descending stairs); weakly abducts. Fourth nerve palsy causes vertical diplopia and a compensatory head tilt away from the lesion.
Superior oblique muscle.blood_supply: Muscular branches of the ophthalmic artery.
